title: Applied ML Evals: Comprehensive Integration Playbook (Eval Harness, Prompt Sets, Onboarding, Guardrails, Quantization, Regression)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood's applied-ML evaluation artifacts and processes: the eval harness, prompt set and benchmark standards, model onboarding checklists, quality guardrails, quantization profile guidance, and the regression triage workflow. It is intended for ML engineers, applied ML reviewers, SREs supporting model serving, and solutions engineers that onboard customer models.

Goals

- Provide a single operational reference for end-to-end evals and regression handling.
- Ensure consistent prompt sets and metrics across model rollouts.
- Reduce the mean time to detect and remediate quality regressions.
- Provide safe quantization profiles and rollback guidance that balance cost and fidelity.

Scope

This document covers: eval harness integration, standards for prompt sets/benchmarks, model onboarding and automated checks, guardrail thresholds and monitoring, quantization profile lifecycle, and triage steps for regression incidents. It does NOT include research-level metric definitions or dataset licensing guidance (see related pages).

Ownership and Roles

- Applied ML (owner): responsible for prompt set curation, eval harness test suites, and quality thresholds.
- Serving Runtime (owner): ensures CI integration for models, perf/latency regression detectors, and rollout hooks.
- Product/Platform: approves customer-facing guardrail SLAs and sign-off for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- SRE: implements alerting and escalation for production regressions.

Eval Harness Integration

Summary

The eval harness is the canonical test runner for unit and integration evaluations of models that will serve on Redwood. It runs locally, in CI, and as a periodic job in the evaluation cluster. The harness supports reproducible prompt execution, deterministic RNG seeds for sampling, multi-model comparisons, and artifact storage to S3-backed evaluation buckets.

Required checks (CI gates)

1. Unit tests for prompt formatting and tokenization fixtures.
2. Baseline metric check: new model must report within +/-X% of the baseline on core metrics (see "Quality Guardrails" below).
3. Safety filter regression: zero increase in disallowed output rate above configured threshold.
4. Quantization smoke test (if signed off): end-to-end generation throughput and quality delta check.

Run commands (examples)

- Local: ./eval-harness/run.py --suite core --model-path /models/local/my-model --seed 42
- CI: make eval CI_MODEL=my-model CI_SUITES=core,robustness
- Periodic: airbyte job triggers eval-harness 'nightly-regression' suite and stores results to s3://redwood-evals/nightly/<date>/

Prompt Sets and Benchmark Standards

Standards

- Single-responsibility prompts: each prompt targets one capability (e.g., summarization, question-answering, instruction-following).
- Metadata: every prompt must include tags (capability, difficulty), origin, expected outputs, and canonical verdict criteria.
- Versioning: prompt sets are versioned with semver and immutable once released; corrections create a new patch version.

Minimum fields for prompt JSON record (example schema serialized as text)

- id: unique-id-string
- text: prompt text with clear placeholders
- tags: ["summarization","sensitivity-low"]
- expected_behavior: short text description
- failure_modes: list of known failure cases
- author: name and team
- created_at: YYYY-MM-DD

Benchmarks and Baselines

- Baseline bundles: curated set of prompt-sets per capability (core, robustness, safety, hallucination).
- Metric families: accuracy/EM, ROUGE/BLEU for text tasks, semantic-similarity using embeddings for paraphrase checks, and calibrated safety scoring.
- Baseline capture: maintain a baseline artifact for each model-family and benchmark version in the eval artifact store.

Model Onboarding Guide (step-by-step)

1. Pre-onboarding checklist (owner: Applied ML)
   - Confirm licensing and model provenance.
   - Add model metadata to model-catalog: architecture, tokenizer, expected seq-len, vRAM, training corpus tags.
2. Local evaluation (owner: model author)
   - Run eval harness with 'core' and 'safety' suites.
   - Produce artifact: metrics.json, examples/failures.json, hallucination-report.md.
3. CI and canary stage (owner: Serving Runtime)
   - Create rollout candidate and run regression comparison vs production baseline.
   - Required: pass core-metrics gate and safety gate, and report latency p50/p95 within configured thresholds.
4. Stakeholder review (Applied ML + Product)
   - Review artifact and sign off on quality/SLAs.
5. Quantization validation (if applicable)
   - Validate quantized variant against floating-point baseline using 'quant-smoke' suite.
   - Approve profile or reject and iterate.

Quality Guardrails

Core metrics and thresholds (example defaults)

- Functional accuracy: >= baseline - 3% relative (task-dependent).
- Safety: disallowed-output-rate <= baseline + 0.1 percentage points.
- Hallucination (fact-check F1): >= baseline - 5% relative.
- Latency: p95 <= configured SLO (hosted: 500ms, dedicated: 350ms) for 512 tokens.
- Cost per 1k tokens: not to exceed model-family expected unit cost (tracked in Optimize).

Monitoring hooks

- Continuous evaluation: nightly runs against subset of prompt-sets for quick regression detection.
- Drift detection: monitor embedding-distance distributions for prompt categories; alert when mean shift > 3 sigma.
- User feedback loop: ingest labeled failures from customer reports; auto-attach to the next triage cycle.

Quantization Profiles and Guidance

Profile types

- safe-q4_0: conservative 4-bit quantization, recommended for early experiments.
- perf-q4_1: higher throughput with modest accuracy delta; requires quant-smoke pass.
- q8: 8-bit fallback profile for memory-constrained deployments.

Profile lifecycle

1. Drafting: applied-ml creates proposed profile and numeric mapping.
2. Smoke validation: run quant-smoke (see run commands) and compare against floating baseline on core and robustness suites.
3. Sign-off: Applied ML approves and adds profile to model-catalog as an allowed variant.
4. Runtime rollout: Serving Runtime enables on canary traffic with metric gates; monitor for 24-72 hours before full rollout.

Quant-smoke example command

./eval-harness/run.py --suite quant-smoke --model my-model --profile perf-q4_1 --seed 1234

Regression Triage Playbook

Severity levels

- Sev-1 (critical): production-wide quality regression affecting multiple customers or safety violation increase >0.5pp. Immediate rollback and incident page.
- Sev-2 (high): noticeable degradation on a core benchmark or p95 latency breach beyond 2x SLO. Investigate with 4-hour MTTR target.
- Sev-3 (medium): localized regression detected in nightly runs or single-customer report. Triage in next business day.

Triage steps

1. Ingest: Alert generated from monitoring or customer report creates a triage ticket with artifacts (metrics, failed examples, request traces).
2. Quick triage (15-30m): Applied ML + Serving Runtime review to determine scope and severity.
3. Containment: If Sev-1/2, rollback to last known-good model variant and engage incident response.
4. Root cause analysis: run targeted A/B comparisons, token-level diff of outputs, and compare embedding distributions.
5. Mitigation: patch prompt templates, update filter heuristics, or revert quantization profile.
6. Postmortem: document findings, RCA, and remediation steps; map to preventative work (e.g., new unit tests or prompt-set expansion).

Operational Runbook Snippets

- Rollback command (serving runtime CLI): redwoodctl rollout revert --service model-serving --to-version v1.2.3
- Re-trigger eval suite for a given candidate: ./eval-harness/run.py --suite core,robustness --candidate v2.0.1 --output s3://redwood-evals/tmp/v2.0.1/

Examples and Templates

- Prompt set entry example: {"id": "summ-001", "text": "Summarize the following text:
{context}", "tags": ["summarization"], "expected_behavior": "Concise 2-3 sentence summary"}
- Metrics report template: metrics.csv columns = [suite,metric_name,baseline_value,candidate_value,delta,pass_fail]

Governance and Release Policy

- Any model that fails safety or core accuracy gates cannot be rolled to production for hosted or dedicated customers.
- Private deployments may accept exceptions under contract but must document compensating controls and get Security sign-off.

References

- Eval harness standards: applied-ml-eval-harness-standards-2025
- Prompt set guidelines: prompt-sets-and-benchmarks-guidelines-2026
- Quantization best practices: quantization-profiles-best-practices-2026

Appendix: Quick checklist (onboarding)

- [ ] Model metadata added to catalog
- [ ] Core and safety suites pass locally
- [ ] CI comparison against baseline complete and within thresholds
- [ ] Quantization profile validated (if used)
- [ ] Stakeholder sign-off and rollout plan documented

Contact and escalation: applied-ml@redwood.internal, runtime-oncall@redwood.internal
